text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish toymaker Lego is launch a major new campaign in the Far East, Australia and New Zealand with new products specially designed for the Asian market and forming a new sales company, Lego Asia Ltd, the aim being triple sales in the region in the next decade.

---Danish exports to Poland and the Baltic republics of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania have risen 18 percent per year in the 1993-95 period and the trend is continuing this year, buoyed by Danish state support schemes to eastern European countries.

--- Denmark is working on plans to contribute 700 soldiers to the NATO peacekeeping force in Bosnia in 1997. This means that even if NATO decides to cut back present Bosnia IFOR force levels by half in 1997, the number of Danish soldiers will be almost unchanged compared at the present 807 complement.

--- Danish MD Foods dairy group hopes to double sales in Germany within the next decade by launching new products and creating closer relations with German retail chains. Sales in Germany amounted to some 2 billion crowns in 1996. REUTER"
